_what: The agreement between the VESTA Kiosk and the VESTA Agent (the /agent/v1 interface), declared ONCE. The Kiosk's proxy (rootfs/usr/bin/supervisor-proxy.py) checks against it, the app (src/agent/agentApi.ts) reads its lists, and the VESTA Agent host keeps a copy (agent-host/contract/agent-contract.json) that its CI compares with this file. A change a version-1 agent cannot survive is a new version, not an edit to this one.
_moment: How a moment and a day are written in text a person reads, by both apps (owner, 2026-10-29: alert #83 said "24/10/2026 19:05" on Telegram and "2026-10-24 19:05" on the tablet; the owner chose day first, everywhere). strftime directives, only %d %m %Y %H %M: on the villa's clock, the same on every screen whatever the reader's locale.
_entityPattern: An entity id as the VESTA Agent may name one (kiosk-rooms, the villa model): the Kiosk's proxy checks every id against it before it reaches a template. (Until 2.496.445 this sat in `message`, with the message channel the agent never used: /agent/v1/messages and /choices were removed with the Kiosk's agent window.)
_ticketUpdate: One step in a Facility fault's history (FmTicketUpdate in src/fm/fmTypes.ts; the VESTA Agent writes them through /agent/v1/fm-data). `kind` says what the step is, so neither side reads a note's first words: none = a status step (raised, picked up, resolved; `by` the profile that recorded it, `who` the name typed for who does the work); reopened = a resolved fault open again (`by` who reopened it); retitled = the VESTA Agent changed the title (`title` the new one, `was` the one before); reading = what the VESTA Agent reads now on a fault whose title a person changed (`title`): the person's title stays; noted = a line of what happened about the fault on Telegram (a reminder or an escalation sent, a button pressed), `note` its words and `at` when — it changes neither the status nor the title, and a Kiosk lists it in /agent/v1/info `step_kinds` before the VESTA Agent writes one; cleared = resolved with no work done (the Kiosk's "Close — no action needed", the agent's own clearing of a problem gone) — never a repair in any figure. A step the VESTA Agent writes carries `title` when it gives the fault one, and `was` when it changes it. A completion the agent writes for a person's Done carries `who`, the person (its `by` is the agent's, stamped by the Kiosk).

ticketUpdate._kindsBeforeList: The step kinds a Kiosk took before /agent/v1/info listed them (`step_kinds`, 2.496.356): what the VESTA Agent writes to a Kiosk whose info lists none. Another kind is written without its `kind`, or not at all when it is one of `notStatusChanges` (without its kind it would read as a change of status).
ticketUpdate._clearedBefore: A close written before steps carried a kind is a close with no work when its note is one of `clearedNotes` or starts with one of `clearedNotePrefixes` (review 31).
ticketUpdate._histories: How a closed fault was closed, as both Kiosk sides read it (architecture review, 2026-10-15): the app's figures (src/fm/fmEngine.ts lastResolution, isClearedStep) and the proxy's retention (supervisor-proxy.py _fm_last_resolution, _fm_cleared_step, _fm_ticket_expired) — 2.496.372 fixed the same misreading on both. Each case is a resolved fault's `updates`: `last` the index of the step that last resolved it (of the status changes, in time order; a step whose time cannot be read sorts first), null when none did; `cleared` whether that step closed it with no work done; `expired` whether the proxy no longer keeps it at `now` with closes evidenced for `evidenceDays` (0: a repair is kept for ever, a close with no work leaves after 90 days). tests/oracles/fault_close.mjs and tests/store-doors.py drive both sides through every case.

_heartbeat: POST /agent/v1/heartbeat: the VESTA Agent says it is alive. `status`: a short text (at most 200 characters). `cadence` (optional): its own timing, which the Kiosk shows in the Overview's (i) instead of a copy of the defaults (architecture review, 2026-10-15) — `checkMinutes` how often it looks at its alerts and faults (1-1440), `nightlyAt` the villa time of its nightly check (HH:MM), anything else in it is dropped. Without it the Kiosk says no number. Shown only while the Agent is online: once its heartbeats stop (/agent-status `offline`) the Kiosk's proxy answers `cadence: null`, and the Kiosk says "by the VESTA Agent" and "it checks regularly" instead of a stale number. A `cadence` of another shape never refuses the beat: the beat counts (the Agent is online), the timing is dropped (stored null, so the Kiosk gives no number) and the answer carries `"cadence": "refused: <why>"`.
_maintenance: The heartbeat's answer carries `maintenance`: the villa's maintenance mode, switched by the owner in the Kiosk's Advanced Settings › System (owner, 2026-10-29: a switch on the tablet and a mark in its top bar while it is on, so nobody forgets it). While it is true the VESTA Agent sends only urgent (P1) alerts; P2, P3 and P4 are recorded and not sent. The Kiosk owns it, as it owns the devices asleep by design: the Agent keeps the last answer it read, and an answer without the field (an older Kiosk) leaves what it kept. It replaces the villa helper the Agent read before (one switch, one place).
_unavailableByDesign: The heartbeat's answer carries `unavailableByDesign`: the entity ids the villa's owner marked, in the Kiosk's Advanced Settings › Devices › Asleep between reports, as devices that sleep between reports (a battery door sensor goes "unavailable" minutes after each report until it next reports). Their "unavailable" is normal: the Kiosk shows their last report and raises nothing, and the VESTA Agent skips its offline checks for them. The Kiosk owns the list (it is always installed; the Agent may not be): sorted, each id once, matching `entityPattern`, an empty list when none is marked — read from the stored device configuration on every beat (owner, 2026-10-21; added within version 1: an agent that does not read it loses nothing).

fields.cadence: {checkMinutes, nightlyAt, lastLookAt}, optional; lastLookAt (optional) the ISO moment its every-checkMinutes look last started: the card's Next check counts from it

answer.offline_after_minutes: integer: minutes of silence before the Kiosk shows the agent offline
answer.unavailableByDesign: list of entity ids, sorted, each once: the devices asleep by design; [] when none
answer.maintenance: true while the villa's maintenance mode is on (Advanced Settings › System): the Agent sends only P1 alerts; false otherwise
answer.cadence: present only when the beat's cadence was dropped: "refused: <why>"

_ticket: The Facility fault the VESTA Agent writes and reads (/agent/v1/fm-data), declared ONCE (architecture review, 2026-10-15: these were copies on each side, and a renamed stamp would have silently stopped the agent retitling its faults). `agentStamp`: the name the Kiosk's proxy stamps on every step and completion the agent writes, and `source` on every record it creates or changes — the agent tells its own steps from a person's by them. `origins`: where the agent made a fault from (its `origin` field: an alert, its nightly check, a chat's "Create this fault"), the Kiosk's source icon. `checks`: how the agent reads a fault again to close it (its `check` field) — "minutes" at every look (heartbeat.cadence.checkMinutes) — every open nightly-check fault too, closed once no longer found (owner, 2026-10-20) — "nightly" at its nightly check only (heartbeat.cadence.nightlyAt) — the card's "Next check", the soonest of its faults' next reads (owner, 2026-10-15). The Kiosk lists the ones it reads in /agent/v1/info `ticket_checks`; a check it does not list is read at its source's usual clock (a nightly-check fault: at every look). `fields`: what the agent writes on a fault beyond the Kiosk's own — the Kiosk lists the ones it reads in /agent/v1/info `ticket_fields`, and the agent writes a newer one only to a Kiosk that lists it. `takenStep`: a person took the fault on in the Kiosk ("Open Ticket") — a step with status in_progress, no kind, not stamped agentStamp: the agent stops chasing its alert. `sample`: one fault as the Kiosk holds it after the agent made it and a person took it on; both sides read it in their tests.

fields.alertNumber: integer: the alert's number as every chat writes it (#5); alerts only
fields.alertPriority: its alert's priority (P1…P4) as every chat writes it after the number: the label `alertLabel` (#5-P2); alerts only, kept current by the VESTA Agent
fields.check: one of checks; absent on a fault only a person closes (chat)
fields.titlePattern: its title with {since} where a duration goes ("Pump offline for {since}."): the Kiosk words it from `since` each time it shows it; absent when the title holds no duration, or a person retitled it
fields.since: ISO moment that duration counts from (when the device went offline, its last report)
fields.closesAt: ISO moment the VESTA Agent closes it if what it reported stays over (its alert desk's clear wait); absent while it still holds
fields.confirmsBy: on a closed fault the VESTA Agent still watches, WHOEVER CLOSED IT (owner, 2026-10-23: a person's Done or Close; 2026-10-25: every close alike): the ISO moment its watch ends, counted from the close. An alert: the longer of the alert desk's read-again wait after a person's close and its reopen window (the "Watch 1h" its closing line says); a night-check fault: the night check's next run. The fault is resolved as ever (no count, badge, recap or map mark takes it for open); the Kiosk lists it last among the open issues, uncounted, as being confirmed, until the Agent takes the field away once the watch is over (a person's close read again meanwhile: right or cannot tell, it stays closed and watched; still bad, reopened as ever). A reopen by either side removes it. The Agent decides, the Kiosk only shows: never past this moment plus two of the Agent's looks (heartbeat.cadence.checkMinutes), and not past this moment while the Agent is offline, so a watch nobody ends never stays on the screen. Absent on a fault nobody watches, and never written to a Kiosk that does not list it (ticket_fields): that Kiosk resolves it as before

ticket._fieldsBeforeList: The fields of `fields` a Kiosk read before /agent/v1/info listed them (`ticket_fields`, 2.496.382): what the VESTA Agent writes to a Kiosk whose info lists none. Another declared field is not written.
ticket._checksBeforeList: The checks of `checks` a Kiosk read before /agent/v1/info listed them (`ticket_checks`, 2.496.429): what the VESTA Agent writes to a Kiosk whose info lists none.

sample.note: What to do: Power and network of the device named, until it is back.

ticket._alertLabel: How an alert is named everywhere, Telegram's title and the tablet's lines alike (owner, 2026-10-28: "consistency everywhere"): {number} and {priority}; without a priority, `alertLabelNoPriority`.
ticket._priorities: The priorities an alert can carry, most urgent first: the one list both sides check a priority against (the VESTA Agent's vesta_shared.result.PRIORITIES, pinned equal by its tests).

_duration: How long something lasted, in the words BOTH apps write (architecture review round 2, 2026-10-16: the Kiosk's chartUtils.fmtDuration and the VESTA Agent's timeutil.lasting each had a rule, and the weekly report's "Lasted" column a third: 89s read "1min", "89s" and "89s"; 2h 29min "2h 29min", "2h 29min" and "2.5h"). The rule (owner, 2026-10-24: the unit joined to its number, "1h 30min", "10min", "30s"): rounded to the nearest second; under a minute in seconds, never less than "1s"; from a minute on rounded to the nearest minute; from an hour on "1h 20min"; from a day on days and WHOLE hours, the minutes dropped ("1d 9h" until it is 1d 10h). A half rounds up on both apps. Every case is checked by tests/oracles/duration_words.mjs (Kiosk) and by the VESTA Agent's test_duration_words.py.

_criticalDevices: The villa's critical devices: ONE list, the one its "critical devices offline" rule watches (owner, 2026-10-18 — architecture review, offline devices #2: the Kiosk, the agent's night check and its reports each had their own idea). Every automation built from the blueprint whose file name (its path's last part, without .yaml) is `blueprint` names them in its input `input` (one id or a list); the list is the union. The Kiosk's proxy reads it (GET /critical-devices) and the VESTA Agent reads the same; a critical device offline is red (danger), any other offline device amber.
_asked: A kept record that once offered buttons and was rewritten (a villa announcement or a VESTA message, one line per key): the add-on stamps `asked: true` on the rewrite (supervisor-proxy.py _announcements_with; a writer's own `asked` is dropped). The tablet reads it with the buttons it offers now: one that asked and offers none any more is FINISHED (src/messages/messagesModel.ts placeOf: an approval approved, refused or expired, a ring opened or missed; listed under Closed, owner 2026-10-29). An alert is placed by its stage instead.
_vestaMessage: A message the VESTA Agent wrote on Telegram, kept for the tablet AS IT STANDS NOW (ticket 25 of "One inbox", 2026-10-28): POST /agent/v1/vesta-message, one record per thread, added or REPLACED by `key` (never removed by the Agent; the Kiosk tidies it after the records-kept days) and served to every profile at /vesta-messages. `key`: the thread (an incident — `incidentKey` with its number, the one form both sides write and read —, an approval, a snapshot, or one note); `title`, `roles` (who it is for), `to` (the "To:" line as Telegram shows it: the tablet shows it as written), `lead`, `body`, `status` (the lines of its Status: the history, then where it stands), `stage` (new, existing, watch, closed, or none), `mark`, `buttons` ([{label, kind, id}]: the Agent's own button kind and id, never a device or a command; a rewrite without buttons withdraws them), `at` (when the Agent drew it), `languages` ({code: {body, status}} where the Agent holds the words in another language) and `buttonKinds`: each button kind's rules for the tablet, read by both sides: `acts` (it acts or records something: never offered to, and refused from, a guest) and `confirm` (the question the tablet asks before sending it, in the confirmation box it uses for every tap that cannot be taken back). `takes` (the villa's own messages it took over: the runs of the announcements, their `run`, that this card stands for on the tablet) and `photo` (the picture as base64, JPEG or PNG; a rewrite that sends none keeps the first one's). A REPORT (ticket 20 of "One inbox": a note the Agent sent on its own from a scheduled job: the morning digest, the weekly and monthly reports, the owner's weekly lines, the night check's message) also names `report` (that job, as the Agent names it: the tablet lists it under Reports, not Notifications), `page` (the id of its HTML page, uploaded first to /agent/v1/fm-document: kept while a kept message names it, then the records-kept days, never with a ticket), `language` (the code of the language its words are in: English when the Agent wrote it in English) and, per other language in `languages`, its `page` too. `keptOnRewrite`: what a rewrite that names none keeps of the record it replaces (the photo, a report's page and job) — read by the Kiosk and by the Agent's test Kiosk alike; `languages` is not in it: a rewrite drops the words it no longer holds. `limits` are the longest each may be: a longer text is cut, a longer list keeps its first entries (`takes`: its newest, the runs the tablet still holds); the Agent reads them from here. An older Kiosk has no such route (404) and the Agent drops the record.

a.confirm: Approve or refuse this request? It cannot be taken back.

_conversation: Talking to VESTA on the tablet (ticket 21 of "One inbox", 2026-10-29). ⚠️ THE KIOSK NEVER CALLS THE AGENT: a question typed on a tablet is kept in an inbox the Agent collects (GET /agent/v1/inbox?after=<seq>, held open up to `waitSeconds` until one comes: {asks: [{seq, at, profile, text}], last, first}), and VESTA's answers are written back as conversation turns (POST /agent/v1/conversation-turn), which the tablet reads at /vesta-conversation. `profile` is the signed-in profile, STAMPED BY THE KIOSK'S PROXY from the session, never sent by the page; `profiles` maps each profile to the role the Agent answers it with (owner, fm, or guest: answers only, no tool that acts, no approval). One conversation per profile, apart from every Telegram chat. A question is answered only while it is younger than `askKeptSeconds` (the inbox keeps none longer; the tablet then says no answer came); a profile asks at most `asksPerMinute` questions a minute (each costs an AI answer). A PRESS on one of VESTA's buttons (ticket 22 of "One inbox") is collected the same way: an ask with `press` {key, kind, id} instead of `text` (the record it was pressed on: a kept VESTA message, or a turn of the presser's own conversation; the Kiosk accepts only a button that record offers, and from a guest only one whose kind does not act: vestaMessage.buttonKinds), answered by a turn whose `answers` is the press's number (its short answer, as a Telegram toast; the tablet shows it under the button, never as a line of the conversation). A turn: `key` (the Agent's own: one record per key, a rewrite REPLACES it, so a "being prepared" answer becomes its result; `ask:` keys are the proxy's, for the person's own questions, and refused from the Agent), `profile`, `text`, `at`, `photos` (the camera pictures the answer carries, base64 JPEG or PNG, at most `limits.photos`), `page` (an HTML page uploaded first to /agent/v1/fm-document), `buttons` (as a VESTA message's: [{label, kind, id}]; a rewrite without them withdraws them), `answers`, `typing` (true: VESTA is answering in this conversation — Telegram's "typing…" — one record per profile, key `typing:<profile>`, said again every minute while it works and withdrawn (`gone`) when it stops; a tablet trusts it `typingSeconds` after it was last said) and `gone` (true: the answer was withdrawn, as a deleted Telegram message: the tablet no longer shows it). Kept the records-kept days. A SPOKEN question (ticket 23 of "One inbox", hold to talk): the tablet uploads a WAV of `voice.rate` Hz, 16-bit, mono, at most `voice.seconds` long (no other format: the villa's Whisper reads it as it comes); the ask then carries `voice` (the sound's name) instead of `text`, and the person's line `voice: true` with no words yet. The Agent fetches the sound ONCE (GET /agent/v1/voice/<name>, audio/wav: gone after, a voice being the person's; never kept past `askKeptSeconds`) and writes the words it heard onto that line, once: a turn {key: "ask:<seq>", profile, heard} (the only write the Agent may make to an `ask:` key, and only to a spoken line of that profile with no words yet). An older Kiosk has no such routes (404): the Agent collects nothing.

conversation._turnExamples: What a turn may hold, by example (architecture review R, 2026-10-29: the add-on's rule, the page's reading and the Agent's test copy of the add-on had each written it down apart). Both apps replay them: the Kiosk through its own door (tests/agent-interface.py), the Agent through its test copy of the add-on (tests/test_contract_turns.py). `kept`: the add-on keeps it (200) or refuses it (400). `keys`: the kinds of key, by their start: `ask` the person's own lines (the add-on's), `turn` an answer, `press` a press's short answer, `typing` VESTA answering. Profile ops: the Kiosk replays them after the checks that read its conversation.

turnExamples.why: a rewrite of that answer (a being-prepared answer becomes its result)

_stageMarks: What starts an alert's bottom line, by its stage (review Q 3, 2026-10-28): the VESTA Agent writes it (vesta_shared/message_format.py STAGE_ICONS, and the villa's message template it generates) and the Kiosk reads an announcement's stage back from it (src/messages/announcements.ts stageOf): new, existing, and the two ends, watch (cleared, still watched) and closed. Read from here by both: a mark changed on one side alone made a cleared alarm read as new on the tablet.
